sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.571 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Gonda.
3. In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married to the applicant in the year 2019 and on 5.12.2022, his daughter was killed by the matrimonial family members.

sentences.text: 1 4. Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn my attention to the postmortem report which reveals the cause of death as Asphyxia due to ante mortem hanging and apart from a ligature mark, one contusion injury was observed on the right side , lateral aspect of right arm.

It is further argued that the co-accused Nirhu vide order dated 15.02.2024 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.10124 of 2023 and the co-accused Anil vide order dated 19.12.2023 passed in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.13464 of 2023 have been enlarged on bail.
5.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.10124 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No.13464 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail by arguing that the death occurred within three years of the marriage and considering the nature of the offence, the bail application deserves to be rejected.
6. Considering all these facts coupled with the there is no specific allegation against the applicant to demonstrate that soon before the death, the deceased was subjected to any physical or mental torture in relation to demand of dowry at the instance of the applicant, who is the husband of the deceased; two co-accused have already been enlarged on bail; the applicant is in custody since 26.12.2022 having no criminal history, and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
7.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

8. Let the applicant Sahdev be released on bail in the abovesaid first information report number on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
